subject: Re: Model fit evaluation & parity thresholds — PayGrid next steps
messages:
From: Sam Carter <sam.carter@paygrid.com>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Nina O'Connor <nina.oconnor@paygrid.com>
Date: 2027-04-22T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Initial discovery recap — model fit & parity thresholds

Hi Lauren,

Thanks again for the demo this morning — it was helpful to see Redwood's serving and routing options. Per our call, here's a short recap and what PayGrid needs to move forward: 

- Primary goal: replace parts of our customer support triage with an LLM that matches or exceeds our in-house baseline (PayGrid-Large) on intent accuracy and summarizes disputes.
- Acceptance thresholds: >=95% intent accuracy on our core prompt set; no more than 2% degradation on critical F1 metrics compared to baseline.
- Non-functional: 99th percentile latency <400ms for single-turn classification, and budget target ~ $0.0008/token (we can be flexible if latency improves).
- Data: we'll share a 2k prompt/dev set (anonymized) and the evaluation labels. See attached sample prompts.
- Security: must support private deployment or dedicated capacity for PII-containing flows; SOC2 and audit logs required.

Next steps from PayGrid: please send recommended model candidates (open-model options + Redwood-provided variants), an evaluation plan with metrics and timelines, and a link to the prompt/eval harness you plan to run. We'd like to see a short preview within 48 hours and a full parity report within two weeks if possible.

Best,
Sam

--
Sam Carter
Head of Product, PayGrid

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-04-22T13:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Eval plan & recommended models for PayGrid

Thanks Lauren — putting a quick plan here. High-level recommendations (open models vs proprietary baselines):

1) Candidate models to prioritize (fast pass):
   - Mistral-1.2 (7B/12B variants) — strong instruction-following and lower token cost; good for classification and summarization with prompt engineering.
   - Llama3-13B-instruct Q4 variant (8-bit quant) — good balance of quality/latency for summarization tasks.
   - MPT-30B-instruct (quantized) — if PayGrid is willing to accept higher cost for exemplar quality on edge-case summarization.
   - Redwood-Baseline-L (our tuned proprietary variant) — we should include this as the baseline for parity comparisons.

2) Evaluation metrics & acceptance thresholds (aligning with PayGrid ask):
   - Intent accuracy (primary): target >=95% vs PayGrid baseline.
   - F1 (critical labels): <=2% absolute degradation allowed.
   - ROUGE-L / Summary adequacy (for dispute summaries): acceptance threshold relative to baseline: >=0.98 parity multiplier.
   - Latency: report p50/p95/p99. If open model meets quality but misses latency, show quantized-run numbers and dedicated GPU throughput.

3) Quality regression risks to flag:
   - Prompt sensitivity: some open models require prompt templating to match PayGrid's annotation style; raw prompts may underperform.
   - Tokenization differences: numeric IDs and transaction codes may be tokenized differently across models — we'll add normalization to the harness.
   - Edge-case hallucination on long context — we'll include targeted stress prompts.

4) Eval plan & timeline:
   - Day 0 (today): run quick-pass on 200-sample subset and share preview (metrics + 20 example outputs).
   - Day 2-6: full run on 2k labeled set across 4 model candidates + Redwood baseline; collect metrics and per-example diffs.
   - Day 7-10: analysis, regression triage, and recommended deployment configuration (quantization, batch sizes, runtime knobs).

5) Attachments & links: I've attached a preview spreadsheet (eval_results_preview.xlsx) with the 200-sample quick-pass. I'll upload the full harness and the run configs to the Drive link Lauren will share.

Next steps for Sales/SE: Lauren pair with Aditya to confirm provisioning (dedicated vs private) and any compliance paperwork. For PayGrid: please confirm you can share the full 2k labeled set by EOD tomorrow and whether you'd prefer us to run on Redwood Dedicated or in your VPC.

Marissa

Sam/Nina — quick update and mutual action plan: 

- We received the 2k labeled set and the sample prompts. Thank you.
- Marissa's team ran the 200-sample quick-pass; attached is the preview. Early signal: Mistral-1.2 and Redwood-Baseline-L are within ~1.5% on intent accuracy on this small slice; more variation on summaries (we need the full run).
- Next concrete steps:
   1) We will run the full parity report on Redwood Dedicated capacity (recommended) unless you confirm Private VPC today. Dedicated gives faster turnaround (2-4 business days).
   2) We'll provide a per-model parity dashboard and a short executive summary when the full run completes.
   3) If any model shows >2% degradation on critical F1, we'll propose mitigation: prompt template tweaks, small calibration dataset fine-tune (few-shot), or switching to the Redwood-Baseline-L variant.

Please confirm Dedicated vs Private and any procurement steps we should loop in (PO, SOW). We're targeting the full report by end of next week if Dedicated is approved.

Best,
Lauren
